newsitem.title: USA: Tax agents seize Texas home of missing atheist.
newsitem.headline: Tax agents seize Texas home of missing atheist.

text.p: U.S. Internal Revenue Service agents on Tuesday seized the $231,000 Austin home of Madalyn Murray O'Hair, who disappeared in August 1995.
O'Hair, who won the landmark U.S. Supreme Court decision in 1963 calling for an end to school prayer, owes $250,000 in back taxes, an IRS spokesman said.
Agents removed furniture and personal property from the home and evicted Spike Tyson, a member of O'Hair's non-profit organisation, American Atheists Inc., who has been living in the house.
O'Hair, her granddaughter, Robin Murray-O'Hair, and son, Jon Murray, disappeared after telling associates they were headed to New York to protest the visit of Pope John Paul II.

A typewritten note was left on the organisation's door telling the staff they had been laid off. The family dogs were dropped off at a boarding kennel where family members said they would return to pick them up later.
IRS rules call for O'Hair's property to be sold at auction in 45 days unless she emerges to settle the tax levy.

O'Hair's estranged son, William Murray, a Washington-based Christian activist and founder of the God Is Not Government organisation, has filed a missing person's report with Austin police. Earlier this year, Murray abandoned his attempts in Austin probate court to seize control of his mother's assets.

Robin Murray-O'Hair's sports car was found at the Austin airport in October 1996, 14 months after the trio disappeared, but police said they have no evidence of foul play in connection with the disappearance and continue to investigate.

O'Hair's disappearance has spawned several theories floated by supporters and detractors, including one that O'Hair died following a deathbed conversion to Christianity and another that the three key officers of American Atheists Inc. had fled to New Zealand.
